speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, I need to know more about the onset of your symptoms. When did you first notice the weakness in your right leg and the unsteady gait?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. I understand the acute onset of the leg weakness and gait issues, alongside the 6-month history of cognitive and behavioral changes. Do you have any history of recent head trauma, seizures, or exposure to specific toxins?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of cognitive decline, behavioral changes, and acute focal weakness, I need to rule out structural causes like a tumor or vascular event. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI_With_Contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI shows nonenhancing white matter lesions, which suggests a demyelinating or inflammatory process rather than a tumor. Have you experienced any visual disturbances, such as double vision or temporary loss of vision, in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient's HIV status combined with non-compliance and white matter lesions strongly suggests HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder or an opportunistic infection like PML. REQUEST TEST: HIV_Viral_Load_and_CD4_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HIV Viral Load: > 100,000 copies/mL, CD4+ Count: 56/μL

speaker: Doctor
text: The severely low CD4 count and high viral load, combined with the MRI findings of nonenhancing white matter lesions, are classic for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
